Error.description: Every refusal, whatever route it came from.

code.description: Stable and typed: what a program branches on.

next_steps.description: Calls that would work, each a sentence.

retry_after_ms.description: How long to wait before the same call works.

revoked_at_ms.description: When the key was revoked, for `key_revoked`.

action.description: The action refused, with what it takes, for an action's refusal.

kind.description: `read`, `undoable` or `outside`: what running it may reach.

result.description: The JSON schema of what it answers, where it declares one.

schema.description: The JSON schema of the value, where the app gives one.

Param.description: One parameter of an action, as its app publishes it.

key.description: What the key sent reaches, when one was sent.

scope.description: `all` or the one workspace it reaches.

created_by.description: The person's device that approved it.

expires_at_ms.description: `null` for a key that lasts until revoked.

id.description: What every route names it by.

host.description:
The host that keeps it: a server's name, or the person's device that
hosts it; absent while none of their devices said.

role.description: `owner` for one of the person's own, else the role they hold there.

labels.description:
What the person labelled it with when they made it (`customer_id` →
`cus_8121`), read by their own keys alone.

unattended.description:
Keys made for this workspace alone run commands in its Linux machine
without asking the person each time; absent while they are asked, as
every workspace starts. Read by the owner's keys alone.

own.description: One of the person's own, rather than one they were invited into.

kept_here.description: Whether the device answering keeps a copy of it.

Workspace.description:
A workspace as the account lists it: what `/v1` answers, and what an MCP
client and the desktop read of the person's workspaces.

path.description: The path listed; `apps` for the apps.

actions.description: The actions of the resource listed.

kinds.description:
The actions the rows offer, once for each kind of row: a row names
those it offers by id.

next_cursor.description: Passed back as `cursor` for the rest.

id.description: The resource's own id, which names it whatever else is titled the same.

key.description: The app's stable key for it, the name its actions answer it by.

kind.description: The app's type of it, or `app`.

has_children.description:
Whether a query with this row as its parent answers rows the workspace
holds now. An app holding no document here says no, though listing it
would start it on a new one; a walk reads what is there and starts
nothing.

reads.description:
Whether a read answers the row as a resource of its own. A row that is
only a place inside it (an option or a choice, like a reading font or a
built-in folder) is part of what lists it and is never read alone; a
listing that does not say is read as it always was, every row read.

actions.description:
The ids of the actions it offers, each described once in the
listing's `kinds` under the row's `kind`.

Row.description: One row of a listing: a resource under the path listed, or an app.

fields.description: The app's own fields, with its own types.

cursor.description: The app's cursor for the next page.

surface.description:
For an app: its surface in the form it is kept by
(`collab_types::surface::canonical`), what types are generated from.

surface_version.description: For an app: its surface's version, `<app>@<digest>`.

item.description: The key a read takes it by.

Child.description: A list of what a resource holds, one entry of it.

status.description: `ok`, `pending` or `cancelled`. (A failure is the error shape.)

path.description: The action at the resource it resolved to, `app/resource#action`.

result.description: The action's output, as the app typed it.

made.description:
What it made, each with its id and the address it is published under:
every item a write of several made, not only the first.

link.description: The link to the record it changed.

links.description: Every record it changed, once each.

edited_by_person.description: What actually ran, when the person changed the arguments first.

ask.description: What the person is being asked, while it waits for them.

undone.description: What was undone, for an undo.

ActionAnswer.description: An action's answer, and an invocation's.

Made.description: An item a write made: its id, and the address it is published under.

url.description: Where the person answers it, when a page for it exists.

Ask.description: What the person is asked before an action runs.

text.description:
The lines, in reading order, one node each:
`<role> "<name>" = "<value>" [state]`, indented by depth.

app.description: The app whose window shows it.

shown.description: Whether the lines are of the resource or of the window it could not show.

tree.description: The same view as a tree: each node's role, name, value, state, bounds and action.

viewport.description: The view's size, in logical pixels.

window_origin.description: Where the view stands in the app's window, in logical pixels.

revision.description: The revision of the document the view shows.

picture.description: Where the picture is kept, as a content address, when one was asked for.

View.description:
What an app's window shows for a resource: its view's semantic lines, the
same ones an MCP client's `tilo_view` prints, and a picture with `picture`.

session.description:
The program session it continues, as an earlier answer named it: the
`let`s its programs bound, the references its answers showed (`n3`),
and the steps `undo` and `history task` take back and list. Without
it the program starts a new session.

status.description:
`ok`, `waiting` (for its person's yes: `text` names where they answer, and it runs
once they approve) or `failed`.

output.description: The program's answer, a line per element.

detail.description: Why it failed: the trap's words, or what did not compile.

steps.description: Every step of the run that changed something, oldest first.

text.description:
What a person reads: the answer's lines, each resource by its
reference (`n3`).

session.description:
The program session it ran in: send it with the next program to
continue it.

size.description: How many bytes the whole file is.

offset.description: How many of them are there: the next piece goes at this offset.

PutContent.description:
A content put: where an unfinished one stands, and what every byte of it
is once the last piece answered.

id.description: The cursor after it: `Last-Event-ID` resumes there.

data.description: The event as its kind gives it.

Event.description: One event of a workspace's stream, or of a webhook's delivery.

messages.description:
The conversation: each `{"role", "content"}`, the role `system`,
`user`, `assistant` or `tool`.

tools.description:
The tools the model may call, each `{"name", "description",
"input_schema"}`.

max_output_tokens.description: The most tokens the answer may take.

ModelAsk.description:
One turn asked of the person's own model, which the server that keeps
their workspace asks with the key their vault keeps there: the
conversation as the model service takes it. The answer streams as
server-sent events: `text` and `reasoning` each carry `{"text": …}`, what
the model wrote since the event before; `answer` ends the stream with the
whole turn, `{"Ok": {"message", "stop_reason", "usage"}}` or
`{"Err": {"kind", "message"}}`, the kind telling a caller what to do
(`no_provider`: none set up yet; `authentication`: no key kept); `error`
ends it with a refusal of the API's own shape.

tl.so.tilo.agent.Agents.ask.Arguments.description:
Asks `agent` about the resource the ask is made from (`.made_from(r)`). Whoever makes it
decides first whether the agent may read that resource, and asks with nothing said when it
may not: the ask then says so, and holds nothing of the resource.

An ask made from a resource is named by it and the mention: every device that asks it so
makes the same ask, and asking again is that ask.

A new contact, named by what is typed where they were made; a book's entry gives the name
it takes, so nothing is left called "No name yet" by a person who typed one.

tl.so.tilo.contacts.Book.group.Arguments.description:
Puts a contact in a group, making the group the book's place if it is new: the same group
however it is spelled, so "Work" and "work" are one place.

tl.so.tilo.contacts.Book.new_group.Argum.description: Starts a group the book offers as a place, with nobody in it yet.

tl.so.tilo.contacts.Book.merge_into.Argu.description:
Merges the card that goes into the one that stays: every number, mailbox, address and group of
both is the card that stays, the fields `take` names come from the card that goes, and the
card that goes is deleted. One change, so undo brings both cards back.

tl.so.tilo.contacts.Book.export_book.Arg.description: Every contact as one vCard file, which another address book reads whole.

tl.so.tilo.contacts.Book.import_vcard.Ar.description:
Imports the contacts a vCard file holds into the book, each card a contact of its own, and
answers how many were added. A file whose cards cannot be read adds nothing and changes
nothing: what it says is the refusal.

tl.so.tilo.contacts.Book.add_contacts.Ar.description:
The cards `cards`, the words of a vCard file, as contacts of this book, and how many named
somebody: what an importer, an agent or a script hands a book in one call.

tl.so.tilo.contacts.Book.add_card.Argume.description:
The contact a vCard card says, made in the book, or none for a card that names nobody. Its
rows are filled after it stands in the book, as every resource's are.

tl.so.tilo.contacts.Book.find_for_addres.description:
The contact the book holds for `address`, as an action: what a person, an agent or another
app asks before they write to it. Nothing is changed and nothing is guessed from a name.

tl.so.tilo.contacts.confirm.Arguments.description:
Binds `account` of `service` to the person: the directory's `confirm-endpoint`, or
`confirm-account` where the service names an account scope.

tl.so.tilo.contacts.change.Arguments.description:
Changes the account an association names, under the directory's rule that a changed address
needs review before anything is sent to it.

tl.so.tilo.contacts.forget.Arguments.description:
Takes an association away: messages from that account stop reaching this contact, and what was
already received is unchanged.

tl.so.tilo.contacts.share.Arguments.description:
Shares this card with the workspace's apps, under the person it is: the name, the numbers and
the mailboxes another app reads of a contact before it writes to them.

tl.so.tilo.contacts.unshare.Arguments.description:
Takes the contact out of the directory, leaving its card in the book: what the apps read of it
stops naming it.

Answers the conversation's newest message, to whoever wrote it, quoting it under what is
written.

tl.so.tilo.mail.Thread.reply_all.Argumen.description: Answers the conversation's newest message, to everyone it went to, quoting it.

tl.so.tilo.mail.Thread.forward.Arguments.description:
Sends the conversation's newest message on, with its sender, what it says and the files it
came with.

tl.so.tilo.mail.Thread.archive.Arguments.description: Archives the conversation: its messages leave the inbox.

tl.so.tilo.mail.Thread.to_inbox.Argument.description:
Moves the conversation back to the inbox, and unmutes it: what a person brings back is what
they want to see again.

tl.so.tilo.mail.Thread.move_to.Arguments.description: Moves the conversation to another mailbox of its account.

tl.so.tilo.mail.Thread.delete.Arguments.description: Deletes the conversation: its messages go to the trash.

tl.so.tilo.mail.Thread.purge.Arguments.description:
Deletes the conversation's trashed messages for good, from its server too, and the
conversation with them when no message of it is left. This is the one deletion there is no
trash to take back from: what is deleted for good is gone from the server, and the platform
takes back this app's record of it only.

tl.so.tilo.mail.Thread.snooze.Arguments.description:
Puts the conversation away until a moment: it leaves the inbox, and comes back once that
moment has come, with no window open. The moment is a field, so it survives closing and
reopening, and an agent snoozes the same way.

tl.so.tilo.mail.Thread.snooze_an_hour.Ar.description: Puts the conversation away for an hour, the snooze people reach for most.

tl.so.tilo.mail.Thread.snooze_until_tomo.description: Puts the conversation away until tomorrow morning, at nine, in the person's own zone.

tl.so.tilo.mail.Thread.unsnooze.Argument.description: Brings a snoozed conversation back now, whatever its moment was: it is in the inbox again.

tl.so.tilo.mail.Thread.label.Arguments.description:
Gives the conversation a label, or takes one away: `on` says which. The label joins the
workspace's labels the first time it is given, so it has a filter of its own from then on.

tl.so.tilo.mail.Thread.mute.Arguments.description:
Mutes the conversation, or unmutes it: a muted one stays out of the inbox until it is
brought back, whatever its new messages do.

tl.so.tilo.mail.Thread.mark_read.Argumen.description: Marks the conversation read, or unread again.

tl.so.tilo.mail.Thread.answer.Arguments.description:
Answers the conversation with what was typed: the message goes to whoever wrote its newest,
as a reply to it, quoted.

tl.so.tilo.mail.Message.export_eml.Argum.description:
The message as an `.eml` file, which every mail program opens. A message taken in from outside
an account's server is exported as it was sent; one its server holds is written from what the
workspace keeps of it.

tl.so.tilo.mail.Message.reply_to.Argumen.description: Answers one message of the conversation, to whoever wrote it, quoting it.

tl.so.tilo.mail.Message.reply_all_to.Arg.description: Answers one message of the conversation, to everyone it went to but the person answering.

tl.so.tilo.mail.Message.forward_message..description:
Sends one message of the conversation on, with its sender, when and what it says, and the
files it came with.

tl.so.tilo.mail.Message.attachment.Argum.description:
One file the message came with, as a file of its own: what Save puts in Files, and what an
agent reads or hands another app.

tl.so.tilo.mail.Draft.attach.Arguments.description:
Takes a file along with the message: one the person picks, or one an agent hands over. A
message takes up to sixteen files of up to 32 MB each, as mail servers take them.

tl.so.tilo.mail.Draft.detach.Arguments.description: Leaves a file the message was to take along behind.

tl.so.tilo.mail.Draft.cancel_later.Argum.description:
Brings a message back to the outbox: it was sent to go at a moment still to come, and it is
a draft again, whatever the moment.

tl.so.tilo.mail.Draft.send_later.Argumen.description:
Sends the message at a moment instead of now: it waits in the outbox until then, as the
person's hold makes a message wait, and goes with no window open. Until it goes it can be
taken back, and bringing it back leaves it a draft.

tl.so.tilo.mail.Draft.send_in_the_mornin.description:
Sends the message at nine tomorrow, the moment people reach for most when they write in the
evening and do not want it to arrive then.

tl.so.tilo.mail.Draft.send_from.Argument.description: Sends the message from another workspace account.

tl.so.tilo.mail.Draft.send_as.Arguments.description:
Sends the message as another of its account's names or addresses, `Name <address>`: what a
person writing as a role rather than as themselves chooses. Empty sends as the account's own.

tl.so.tilo.mail.Draft.send.Arguments.description:
Sends the message from its account. It leaves the system, so it goes once, and waits in the
outbox until the server took it; it is held back for the person's hold first, so they can
take it back. The effect is an argument the action records, so the wait survives a window
closing and an agent takes it back the same way.

tl.so.tilo.mail.Draft.undo_send.Argument.description:
Takes back a message that was sent and has not gone yet: it never leaves, and the message is
a draft again, as it was. Once it went it cannot be taken back.

tl.so.tilo.mail.Mail.set_hold.Arguments.description:
Sets how many seconds a sent message waits before it goes, so it can be taken back: no wait
at all at zero.

tl.so.tilo.mail.Mail.new_draft.Arguments.description: Starts a message from the first account.

tl.so.tilo.mail.Mail.draft_message.Argum.description:
Writes a message for the person to read and send: to whom, its subject and what it says,
answering `in_reply_to` (a Message-ID) when it names one. Every call makes a draft of its own
beside the others; nothing is written over and nothing is sent. Where an agent drafts a
message, the person finds it in Drafts and sends it.

tl.so.tilo.mail.Mail.prepare_calendar_in.description:
Starts a message inviting `to` to an event, its invitation (`calendar_ics`, iCalendar) carried
beside what it says: what Calendar hands Mail for each guest it invites. Nothing is sent; the
person reads it, and sends it.

tl.so.tilo.mail.Mail.deliver_message.Arg.description:
Takes in a message that reached the workspace from outside its accounts' servers: one moved
in from another mail program (`tilo migrate`), or handed over through the API. It is kept
with the mail held outside the accounts, in the conversation it belongs to (`conversation`,
the Message-ID the conversation began with) and the folder it was in, read or not. `from` is
the sender as a header writes it (`Ada Lovelace <ada@example.com>`), and `original` the
content reference of the message as it was sent, less its large parts: `parts` says where
each of those stands in it and which pieces of content it is in, one JSON text each
(`{"at": 120, "size": 4096, "pieces": ["tilo.content:…"]}`). `attachments` are the files it
carries, each content the workspace holds. A message already held under its Message-ID is
answered as it is, so delivering it again keeps it once.

tl.so.tilo.mail.Mail.open_message_file.A.description:
Opens a message kept as a file a mail program writes (`.eml`, a single message of an mbox, or
Apple Mail's `.emlx`): its headers are read, and it is kept with the mail held outside the
accounts, read, in the inbox. The same file opened again is the message already kept.

tl.so.tilo.mail.Mail.rename_label.Argume.description: Renames one of the workspace's labels, all the conversations that carry it with it.

tl.so.tilo.mail.Mail.delete_label.Argume.description: Deletes one of the workspace's labels, and takes it off every conversation that carries it.

tl.so.tilo.mail.Mail.discard.Arguments.description: Throws a message being written away.

tl.so.tilo.notes.Note.new_child.Argument.description:
Starts a note inside `n`'s own, after the notes it already holds, titled `words` when the
caller knows them already (a `/page` in one of `n`'s blocks names the page it makes with the
words that stood there): the note the window has open too, so a person writing one starts the
note it stands under without finding its row. It is `n`'s action, so the window offers it for
the note it shows and its row offers it.

tl.so.tilo.notes.Note.indent.Arguments.description:
Puts a note under the note it stands over, with the notes under it, as `Tab` does in the
tree; with none named, it goes under the note above it.

tl.so.tilo.notes.Note.outdent.Arguments.description:
Puts a note beside the note it stands in, just after it and the notes under it, as
`Shift-Tab` does in the tree.

tl.so.tilo.notes.Note.move_up.Arguments.description:
Puts a note just over the note above it, with the notes under it, as `Alt-Up` does in the
tree; with none named, over the note just above it.

tl.so.tilo.notes.Note.move_down.Argument.description:
Puts a note just under the note below it and the notes under that one, with its own notes
after it, as `Alt-Down` does in the tree.

tl.so.tilo.notes.Note.add_text.Arguments.description:
Writes `text` (Markdown) at the end of a note, under what it says already: a line, a list or
a paragraph added to it.

tl.so.tilo.notes.Note.tag.Arguments.description:
Gives a note the tag `tag`, and lists the tag in the notebook when it lists none of that
name yet: a name is how a person, an agent and a script know a tag.

tl.so.tilo.notes.Note.untag.Arguments.description:
Takes the tag `tag` off a note. The notebook keeps listing it, so a person finds it again
for another note; deleting it from the notebook takes it off every note.

tl.so.tilo.notes.Note.find_text.Argument.description:
Finds the words `text` in one note, the case of their letters aside, and answers each
paragraph holding them with its place in the note and its words: what the window's find bar
shows, reachable by an agent or the palette that knows the note but not where in it to look.

tl.so.tilo.notes.Note.react.Arguments.description:
Adds your reaction with an emoji to a note, or takes it back when you had reacted with it: a
press on one of its pills, or the pick of the one its add button opened.

tl.so.tilo.notes.Note.insert_image.Argum.description:
Puts a picture in a note, where its words end, described by `alt` for a reader who cannot see
it: the person picks the file, and the note keeps the address of its content rather than the
picture, and the name it came in as. Nothing in `alt` can end the Markdown a picture is
written with, so a description holding brackets or parentheses still reads as one picture.

tl.so.tilo.notes.Note.keep_image.Argumen.description:
Keeps a picture the editor wrote into a note where the person pasted or dropped it: the note
holds the address of its bytes, and the name it came in as, which an export writes beside it.
`picture` is the editor's word of it: its name, then the address of its content.

tl.so.tilo.notes.Note.export_markdown.Ar.description:
A note as Markdown: its title, then its body, each picture it shows written beside it as
`<note>/images/<name>`, a path another reader of the file follows and this app reads again
as the address of the picture's bytes.

tl.so.tilo.notes.Note.export_note.Argume.description:
A note as a file: its Markdown, and the pictures it shows beside it. A note that shows a
picture is one zip — `Q3 plan.md` and `Q3 plan/images/fox.png` — because Markdown reaches a
picture by a path and by nothing else; a note of words alone is that Markdown itself.

tl.so.tilo.notes.Notebook.new_note.Argum.description:
Starts a note titled `title` and saying `body` (Markdown) when the caller knows them already.
Started from the notebook both are empty: what is typed first names it. It stands under
`parent` (at the top of the tree when none) and — where a caller names the note it belongs
after (`after`) — at that place among the notes there; without one it comes after the notes
already under `parent`, never at the foot of a tree it does not stand in.

tl.so.tilo.notes.Notebook.move_to.Argume.description: Moves a note to a place in the tree: at the end of `parent`'s own, or where `before` stands.

tl.so.tilo.notes.Notebook.move_after.Arg.description:
Moves a note to just after `n` and every note under it: the place a drop after a row asks
for, which names the row it lands after rather than the row after that one.

tl.so.tilo.notes.Notebook.duplicate.Argu.description: Copies a note, with every note under it, just after the one it copies.

tl.so.tilo.notes.Notebook.sort_children..description: Puts a note's own in the order of their titles, once, for a branch that grew out of order.

tl.so.tilo.notes.Notebook.delete.Argumen.description: Deletes a note and every note under it, as one change a person takes back at once.

tl.so.tilo.notes.Notebook.append_to_note.description:
Writes `text` (Markdown) at the end of the note titled `title`, the case of its letters aside:
how an agent or a script that knows a note by its name ("add this to Meeting notes") writes
into it without first looking up which note that is.

tl.so.tilo.notes.Notebook.file_note.Argu.description:
Files a note titled `title` and carrying the tag `name` in one step: what another app writes
down of what it did (Today's morning) without waiting on the note it made to name it.

tl.so.tilo.notes.Notebook.new_tag.Argume.description:
Makes a tag of the notebook named `name`, or gives the one already named that: the name is
what people, agents and scripts know a tag by.

tl.so.tilo.notes.Notebook.rename_tag.Arg.description: Names a tag of the notebook: every note that carries the old name carries the new one.

tl.so.tilo.notes.Notebook.delete_tag.Arg.description:
Deletes a tag of the notebook: no note carries the name any more, and the notebook stops
listing it.

tl.so.tilo.notes.Notebook.export_noteboo.description:
The notebook as a zip, one Markdown file for each note: a note's own under the folder of the
note it stands in, and the pictures it shows in its own `images` folder beside it. That is the
shape the import reads, so the notebook comes back as the tree it is, titles, bodies and
pictures alike.

The notebook as one Markdown document, where each note is a heading one level deeper than
the note it stands under (six at the deepest), its body beneath it and the notes under it
after it, read as one text in the order the tree keeps it.

tl.so.tilo.notes.Notebook.import_markdow.description:
Imports a Markdown file as a note, or opens the note that file already made: a note keeps the
address of the file it came from, so importing the same file twice makes one note. The note
stands under the note of the folder its file's path names — `Q3 plan/Ideas.md` under
`Q3 plan.md` — and at the top of the tree when its path names no folder. Its title is the
document's first heading, or the file's name; the heading it says the title with is not said
again in its body.

tl.so.tilo.notes.Notebook.import_page.Ar.description:
Imports a page another service held as a note, keeping whose words it is and where it stood
there: what `tilo migrate` calls for each page it brings over, and what a person's own import
of a file does without a service's words. A page imported by its address there again opens the
note it made, whatever the page says now; the note stands under the note of the folder its
file's path names.

tl.so.tilo.notes.Notebook.import_text.Ar.description:
Imports a note given as words rather than a file: its title, its body as Markdown, the
pictures it shows and the notes its links lead to. A caller holding a page as text — a
script, an agent, a migration — makes the note without writing a file first: `pictures` are
the files the body names as `![alt](name)`, each by the name it came in as, which the note
keeps so an export writes it beside the note again; `links` names, by the path a link leads
to, the note it opens. The note stands at the top of the tree.

tl.so.tilo.notes.Notebook.import_archive.description:
Imports a notebook another tool wrote: a zip of pages, or the JSON a Notion API page listing
answers. A zip comes in under the notebook, a page under the page that held it, in one change:
undo takes the whole import back. That is this app's own notebook written out, a Notion export,
and what `tilo migrate` brings from a wiki: a page per `.md` file, its pictures beside it, and a
database beside it as a `.csv` that becomes a table at its page. Each page's title is its first
heading, or its file's name; the pictures a page shows are the files it stands beside, a
reference read from the page's own folder, and a link to a page of the archive is the reference
to the note that page made. A migration says where each page came from in its own file beside
the pages, and a page that is imported already keeps the note it made. A listing carries no
files, so each of its pages is a note at the top of the tree.

tl.so.tilo.notes.Notebook.import_dropped.description:
Files dropped on the notebook come in one at a time. A Markdown file becomes a note. An
archive or a Notion page listing becomes the pages it holds, whether the notebook's own
written out or another app's export. One action, so undo takes the whole drop back at once.

tl.so.tilo.playback.Playback.play_list.A.description:
Plays the items `items` names, in the order given, from the one at `at`: the queue is what
follows, and the item at `at` plays. The app that calls this fills the title, artist, cover,
source and length it resolves from its own record; the shared actions below move the queue
without reading another app's records.

tl.so.tilo.playback.Playback.set_current.description:
The session shows `item`: its fields are the item's, so a shared next or previous never
leaves the title, cover or source of the one before it.

tl.so.tilo.playback.Playback.set_playing.description: Plays or pauses what plays, as a player's own control and a media key ask it.

tl.so.tilo.playback.Playback.set_length..description: What the player reports of its length, once the decoder knows it.

tl.so.tilo.playback.Playback.remember_po.description:
Keeps the session's place and the item's as `when` records them. It has no effect of its own,
so an app's action that plays can call it inline: an action that needs a moment is a step of
its own, which a nested call only suggests.

tl.so.tilo.playback.Playback.set_positio.description:
Where the player stands, as it reports it, so a later opening resumes there: the session's
place and the item's, kept so another device or a later opening continues from it.

tl.so.tilo.playback.Playback.set_share.A.description:
Where the player stands, as the share of its length a player reports (`0..=1`), kept so a
later opening resumes there.

tl.so.tilo.playback.Playback.resume.Argu.description:
Moves what plays to where `ref` was left, so a video or a song continues where the person
stopped instead of beginning again.

tl.so.tilo.playback.Playback.play.Argume.description: Plays what is chosen, or begins again where it stands.

tl.so.tilo.playback.Playback.pause.Argum.description: Pauses what plays and starts it again where it stood ([`toggle`]'s own job).

tl.so.tilo.playback.Playback.next.Argume.description: The item after this one: the queue's next, or the first when repeat is on.

tl.so.tilo.playback.Playback.select.Argu.description: Plays the queued item at `at`, keeping the queue as it stands.

tl.so.tilo.playback.Playback.seek_by.Arg.description: Moves what plays by `seconds`, for the live card's two seek controls.

tl.so.tilo.playback.Playback.seek.Argume.description:
Moves what plays to `place`, a fraction of its length, and keeps the place so a later
opening continues there.

tl.so.tilo.playback.Playback.mute.Argume.description: Silences the session, or brings back the volume it had.

tl.so.tilo.playback.Playback.shuffle_tog.description: Shuffles the queue, or puts its order back. The item that plays stays first.

tl.so.tilo.playback.Playback.cycle_repea.description: Moves repeat on: off, all, one.

tl.so.tilo.playback.Playback.queue_remov.description: Takes the item at `index` out of the queue.

tl.so.tilo.playback.Playback.queue_move..description:
Moves the item called `from` to stand where `to` stands: the queue row a person dragged,
and the ids its reorder reports.

tl.so.tilo.playback.Playback.add_output..description: Puts the sound on one more place: a speaker in a room, or a cast target.

tl.so.tilo.playback.Playback.remove_outp.description: Takes the place at `index` out of the session; this device is never taken out.

tl.so.tilo.playback.Playback.move_to.Arg.description:
Moves the place at `from` to where `to` is: "continue on the speaker" is moving the session
from this device to it.

tl.so.tilo.playback.Playback.set_output_.description: Sets how loud the place at `index` is.

choice_labels.gnome: The top bar alone; the overview on demand
choice_labels.macos: A floating, rounded, translucent dock at the bottom that hides while a window covers it, and a top bar with the focused app's menus after the system's
choice_labels.minimal: No chrome at rest; the edges reveal what the person needs
choice_labels.tilo: The dock on the bottom with the bar on the top: Tilo's own
choice_labels.windows: A full-width taskbar at the bottom, always shown
choice_labels.windows_desktop: The traditional desktop: frames floating over the shell, the focused window's own commands in the top bar, and a floating dock at the foot, the shape macOS and GNOME people know

tl.so.tilo.shell.Shell.apply.Arguments.description:
Uses the preset `layout`: every setting it names at once. The result is exactly that preset,
so the picker shows it chosen and "custom" is off.

tl.so.tilo.shell.Shell.show_app_menus.Ar.description:
Puts the focused app's menus on the bar, after the system's: what the app in front can do
now, on its resource.

tl.so.tilo.shell.Shell.hide_app_menus.Ar.description: Takes the focused app's menus off the bar.

tl.so.tilo.shell.Shell.reset.Arguments.description: Returns the shell to the preset it was based on, dropping the person's tuning.

tl.so.tilo.shell.Shell.show_bar.Argument.description:
Shows or hides the top bar: the one control that turns it on and off, so a person sees
whether it is on where they press it.

tl.so.tilo.shell.Shell.dock_on.Arguments.description: Moves the dock to `edge`, keeping how it is built.

tl.so.tilo.shell.Shell.show_dock.Argumen.description:
Shows or hides the dock: the one control that turns it on and off, so a person sees
whether it is on where they press it.

tl.so.tilo.shell.Shell.set_dock_running..description: Whether the dock shows the apps running that nobody pinned.

tl.so.tilo.shell.Shell.set_dock_launcher.description: Whether the dock has a launcher entry.

tl.so.tilo.shell.Shell.set_dock_zoom.Arg.description: Whether the dock magnifies the item under the pointer.

tl.so.tilo.shell.Shell.move_part.Argumen.description:
Puts a bar part with the one it comes before, wherever the part stands now: the one action
a drag commits, and the same change from the settings, a shortcut or an agent.

tl.so.tilo.shell.Shell.place_part.Argume.description:
Puts a bar part at `position`, counted from the leading edge: what a drag that names a
place gives.

tl.so.tilo.shell.Shell.show_part.Argumen.description: Shows or hides one part of the bar.

tl.so.tilo.shell.Shell.move_item.Argumen.description: Puts a dock item with the one it comes before: the one action a drag commits.

tl.so.tilo.shell.Shell.place_item.Argume.description:
Puts a dock item at `position`, counted from the leading edge: what a drag that names a
place gives. An item the person's document does not hold yet — an app running on the dock
that they never pinned, which the dock drew from the shell — is pinned where it lands, so
moving an app they already run keeps it on the dock after it closes.

tl.so.tilo.shell.Shell.pin.Arguments.description:
Pins a resource or an app to the dock, before `next` (or at the end when no neighbour is
named): what dragging one onto the dock does, and what the person does from a menu.

tl.so.tilo.shell.Shell.unpin.Arguments.description: Takes an item off the dock.

tl.so.tilo.shell.Shell.open_item.Argumen.description:
What a press on a dock item does, by the app the item stands for: a window of that app on this
screen comes to the front, so the shell says which window the person is in and the top bar's
commands are its own; the window is the one the item was drawn for, so a press never opens a
second copy. An app with no window open is opened (`session.open_app`), and the launcher
shows.

It takes the app's key and not the item: an item the shell's document holds reaches an action as
a document reference, and the press names the one thing it needs, so a run's item reaches it
without a `DockItem` parameter to fit.

tl.so.tilo.shell.Shell.open_style_settin.description:
The style's own settings, and the two ways of changing a style (`docs/designs/app-language/
shell.md` §6): without an agent, in the one place a person's settings live, and with an agent,
by the same actions the person's controls run.

Every setting here is plain tilolang state with a default (`chrome.tl`'s `Shell` document), so
a person who never touches it gets the style as it ships, and the values live in the
layout's own document, synced with the person's devices, with history and undo.

Each setting is one action, so an agent — the canvas conversation or the REPL — changes it
with the same call a press does, attributed and undoable: `shell.set_dock_edge(shell.shell,
edge: shell.Edge.left)`. The style's settings stand over the shell (`style_panel`), opened by
the bar's style menu (`style_menu`, `strips.tl`): a person changes the shell they look at
without leaving it, as `shell.md` §6 asks.

Opens the chosen style's settings over the shell: what the bar's style menu's entry runs, and
what the REPL or the canvas agent calls too.

tl.so.tilo.shell.Shell.show_style_settin.description:
Shows or hides their being open: one control for both, so a person sees the state where they
press it.

tl.so.tilo.shell.Shell.set_strips_tabs.A.description: Whether the strip of several places shows its tab bar: the strips style's own setting.

tl.so.tilo.shell.Shell.set_frames_snap.A.description:
Whether a place let go on the framed canvas lands on the grid: the frames style's own

tl.so.tilo.shell.Layout.a_query_place.Ar.description:
Adds a place showing a search for `text` to `strip`, with the two matches the notes app
answered, and returns the place's key: the state a place stands in until the person chooses

tl.so.tilo.shell.Layout.tab_place_here.A.description:
Tab the place whose window's bar was dragged onto the strip `s` into that strip: a person drags
one window's bar onto another's to make its tabs, and the window's menu's "Move into … as a
tab" runs the same arranging action. The place lands after the strip's other tabs and
comes to the front of them, so the window shows what was dropped on it. A place already in
this strip is only brought to the front, so dropping a window on itself raises it rather than
opening a second place. The strip comes forward with it.

tl.so.tilo.shell.Layout.reorder_place.Ar.description:
Rank the place `place` at `at` among its strip's tabs: what dragging a pill within the
window's bar does, as the shell's own `move` with the place it goes before. The strip reports
the pill's place among the tabs with the moved pill taken out, so the tab it lands before is
that index of the others; the last place goes last.

tl.so.tilo.shell.Layout.bring_forward.Ar.description:
Brings the window of the strip `s` to the front, the keyboard in it: the session brings its
place in front forward, as it does for a press, a script or an agent alike. A strip with no
place has no window to bring.

Shows the shell through the style `style`: a package and a view (`so.tilo.shell:strips`).
Switching keeps the layout: the same places stand where they were, drawn another way.

tl.so.tilo.shell.size_place.Arguments.description:
Gives the place `key` the size a drag of its edge or corner left it at, `size` its width and
height in canvas pixels: one arranging step of the person's, its corner where it stood.

tl.so.tilo.shell.drew_place.Arguments.description:
Keeps how tall the hugging place `key` is drawn now, `size` carrying its height in canvas
pixels as the map lays it out: the free area under it on the canvas is what the person sees
there (canvas.md §1, §7), though the place could grow into it. View state the person's own
canvas reports, never a step of arranging: Undo leaves it alone.

tl.so.tilo.shell.place_dropped.Arguments.description:
Puts a resource dropped on the canvas where it was let go. A place that already stands on the
canvas — the place whose handle was dragged — moves to the point it was let go at, through
its own `position` action, so a drag that ends on the canvas moves the place and never stands
a second one. Any other resource — a message's attachment, a search hit, a row of another
view — is placed at that point through the system's own `place`, which is what an agent's
`place_at` runs. Either is one arranging step of the person's, attributed and undoable.

tl.so.tilo.shell.open_first.Arguments.description:
Enter's work on a query: the first app the text finds opens, so typing "no" and pressing Enter
opens Notes; a query that names no app is what search everywhere answers, as Enter has always
done for what the shell's own rows do not hold.

tl.so.tilo.shell.toggle_vpn.Arguments.description:
Turn the VPN on through its first profile, or off through the one connected: the tile's one
press, whichever way it flips.

tl.so.tilo.shell.a_style_settings.Argume.description:
A shell of one note in the style named, with that place in front, and the style's own settings
open over it: what a person sees who opens them from the bar's style menu.

tl.so.tilo.shell.query_show.Arguments.description:
Show `found` in the place `place` while it shows a query: the same place, now the found
resource (shell.md §8).

tl.so.tilo.shell.query_retry.Arguments.description: Look for what the place `place`'s search names again.

tl.so.tilo.shell.detach_place.Arguments.description:
Give the place `place` a window of its own: what dragging a tab out of its window's bar does,
as the shell's own `split-right` for the window in front. The place stands in front of its new

tl.so.tilo.lang.tasks.Task.due_next_week.description: Makes a task due at the start of next week.

tl.so.tilo.lang.tasks.Task.schedule.Argu.description:
Makes a task due on a day the person picks. Its moment and its reminder move with it, at the
same time of day: a task due Wednesday at six, reminded at six, moved to Friday is due Friday
at six and reminded then.

tl.so.tilo.lang.tasks.Task.set_time.Argu.description:
Sets the time of day a task is due at: the day it is on stays, and a task with no day is due
on the day the moment names. A reminder that was set for the old moment moves with it, as a
day moved by `schedule` keeps its time of day: a task due Wednesday at six, reminded at six,
made seven is due at seven and reminded then.

tl.so.tilo.lang.tasks.Task.due_clear.Arg.description: Clears the day a task is due by: it waits in the inbox, undated.

tl.so.tilo.lang.tasks.Task.remind_at.Arg.description:
Sets the moment whoever is doing a task is reminded of it. A reminder on a day after the task
is due moves the task to that day, its moment with it: being told of a task once its day has
gone is no reminder, so "move the reminder to Friday" moves both.

tl.so.tilo.lang.tasks.Task.remind_clear..description: Clears a task's reminder: it is not told of again.

tl.so.tilo.lang.tasks.Task.remind.Argume.description:
Tells whoever is doing a task, or the one who made it, what it is and when it is due: once,
and not of a task already done. Choosing the notice opens the task.

tl.so.tilo.lang.tasks.Task.set_priority_.description: Sets how much a task matters.
Marks a task as low priority.
Marks a task as medium priority.
Marks a task as high priority.

tl.so.tilo.lang.tasks.Task.file.Argument.description: Files a task under a project the person picks.

tl.so.tilo.lang.tasks.Task.unfile.Argume.description: Takes a task out of its project, back to the inbox.

tl.so.tilo.lang.tasks.Task.assign.Argume.description: Gives a task to someone, or to nobody.

tl.so.tilo.lang.tasks.Task.indent.Argume.description:
Moves a task under the task the view shows just over it in its group, as `Ctrl+]` does; with
none named, under the task above it in the list.

tl.so.tilo.lang.tasks.Task.outdent.Argum.description: Moves a task out from under its parent, just after it, as `Ctrl+[` does in an outline.

tl.so.tilo.lang.tasks.Task.place.Argumen.description:
Puts a task into the list `s` of its project's board (none for the first) at the place `at`
among the tasks already there: what a card's drag names.

Adds a task to the inbox or to `p`, in the list `s` of its board: the entry at a list's end
fills `title` with the words nothing else there takes, and the day, moment and person they
name, so "Call the landlord fri 10am @Bo" is a task due Friday at ten, for Bo.

tl.so.tilo.lang.tasks.Tasks.add_subtask..description:
Adds a subtask under a task, in its project and section, and opens a done one: there is work
under it now.

tl.so.tilo.lang.tasks.Tasks.move_to.Argu.description:
Moves a task to a place in the outline: at the end of `parent`'s subtasks (the top level for
none), or where `before` stands. What is put under a done task opens it.

tl.so.tilo.lang.tasks.Tasks.duplicate.Ar.description: Copies a task, with every task under it, just after the one it copies.

tl.so.tilo.lang.tasks.Tasks.remove.Argum.description: Deletes a task and its subtasks.

tl.so.tilo.lang.tasks.Tasks.clear_done.A.description:
Deletes every finished task and answers how many went: a finished branch goes whole, and a
done task with a step still open under it stays. What was done is the list a person reads
back, so this is no command of the bar.

tl.so.tilo.lang.tasks.Tasks.remove_proje.description: Deletes a project and its sections; its tasks go back to the inbox.

tl.so.tilo.tube.Video.play.Arguments.description: Plays the video, whether or not it was played before.

tl.so.tilo.tube.Video.resume.Arguments.description: Plays the video from where the person left off, when they did not finish it.

tl.so.tilo.tube.Video.progress.Arguments.description:
Records how far into the video the person is, and that they watched it now: it moves to the
front of the history, and asks the service for the address its bytes play from when that is
not known yet. Starting a video, resuming it and moving the playhead as it plays are one
action, so a video has one place it is played from.

tl.so.tilo.tube.Video.forget.Arguments.description: Takes one video out of the person's own history.

tl.so.tilo.tube.Video.retry_playback.Arg.description:
Asks the service for where the video's bytes play from again, after the player could not show
them: the address the client holds is the service's alone to write, and the answer it gives
now is what the player opens.

Deletes the person's own watch history, and the entries carried from before it recorded
members, which this history shows them; nobody else's.

tl.so.tilo.tube.YouTube.set_autoplay.Arg.description:
Each of these keeps one of the person's own playback preferences: the record is theirs, made
the first time they set one, and every other member reads their own.

tl.so.tilo.tube.YouTube.set_speed.Argume.description: How fast videos play for the person: 0.25 to 3, 1 for the usual speed.

tl.so.tilo.tube.YouTube.set_quality.Argu.description: The tallest picture the person wants, as YouTube names it; `auto` takes the best that fits.

tl.so.tilo.tube.YouTube.set_captions.Arg.description: Whether videos show their captions for the person.

tl.so.tilo.tube.YouTube.search.Arguments.description:
Searches YouTube: the service answers with channels, playlists and videos, written where the
search view lists them. The answer arrives through the platform's network, never the app's.

tl.so.tilo.tube.YouTube.end_search.Argum.description:
Leaves the search the feed is showing for the place the person chose: the results stay where
the service wrote them (found again by the query that found them), and the client shows the
place chosen.

tl.so.tilo.tube.YouTube.refresh_feed.Arg.description:
Asks the service for the newest videos of each subscribed channel: what the subscriptions feed
shows.

tl.so.tilo.tube.YouTube.load_trending.Ar.description: Asks the service for the videos it lists as trending.

tl.so.tilo.tube.YouTube.open_link.Argume.description:
Opens a link of the scheme this client claims: the video (`tube:watch?v=<key>`), channel
(`tube:channel?key=<key>`) or playlist (`tube:playlist?key=<key>`) it names, or the search it
asks for (`tube:search?q=<query>`). A shell hands a link here whether or not a window of the
client is open, and what this returns opens in the window. The host publishes it as the
system's `open-link` on the client's root, which is what a shell hands a link to.

tl.so.tilo.tube.YouTube.play_again.Argum.description: Plays the video a history entry names, from where the person left off.

was left. The clip it already made opens instead of a second copy, so its place in history
stays one.

tl.so.tilo.video.Library.delete_playlist.description: Deletes a playlist and the entries that name it.

tl.so.tilo.video.Library.add_bookmark.Ar.description: Bookmarks the moment `at` of `c`, with `text` when the person wrote something.

tl.so.tilo.video.Library.open_dropped.Ar.description:
Opens the videos a person dropped on the window: each file becomes its clip, and the first
plays in the shared session.

tl.so.tilo.video.Library.session.Argumen.description:
The session this app plays through: the one it has, or one made now. It is kept both in
`playing`, which a view reads, and in `sessions`, so the record is a resource of its own.

tl.so.tilo.video.Library.play_clip.Argum.description:
Plays `c` in the shared session, from where it was left (the beginning the first time):
what the window's Play button, the palette and an agent's `play` run. The place is the
shared session's own record, so the video continues on this device or another.

tl.so.tilo.video.Library.restart_clip.Ar.description: Plays `c` from its beginning, as a person who watched it before chooses.

tl.so.tilo.lang.views.Views.write.Argume.description: A view the person writes, kept among their own.

tl.so.tilo.lang.views.Views.discard.Argu.description: Throws a view away, and with it how a type showed through it.

the log recorded them, never who adds it: what it does asks first unless the person trusts
that sender. It is a copy: a later change the sender makes to theirs does not reach it.
